messages:
Priya Das: Quick follow-up from the transparent-fallback RFC — how do we actually wire a \"transparent fallback binding\" into the runtime without exploding telemetry cardinality? Need a plan that gives explainability (which rule fired) but keeps metrics sane.

Jorge Li: short answer: avoid freeform strings in metrics. use small enum codes + route_id. record the decision token only when fallback happens.

Maya Chen: +1. also group reasons into ~6 buckets (capacity, region, model-unavailable, costcap, sla-tier, unknown). That keeps cardinality limited and is still actionable. :thumbsup:

Ken Walker: runtime-wise my worry is extra lookups on the hot path. if we do a policy evaluation and then another binding lookup, we could add ~2-3us per request at p50. can we piggyback the binding decision onto the existing eval pass?

Priya Das: good point. Proposal: policy engine returns a small decision struct: {compat: bool, fallback_code: enum | null, binding_hint: id | null}. only serialize telemetry fields when fallback_code != null. happy path unchanged.

Sam Ortiz: that seems fine. can we see a minimal config snippet? i want to be sure ops can test without touching runtime code.

Jorge Li: sample config prototype (for the console + agent):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  name: default
  fallback_binding:
    mode: transparent
    bucket_map: \"default-buckets-v1\" # server-side mapping of codes -> human text
    emit_on_fallback: true
```

Maya Chen: telemetry example (aggregatable):
```
redwood.routing.fallback{code=\"COSTCAP\", route_id=\"r-1234\", region=\"us-west-2\"} 1
```
We only emit that when fallback occurred. no per-tenant freeform reason.

Ken Walker: ok but the mapping of bucket_map -> human text will need to be versioned so old logs still decode. suggest we include a bundle_version in the decision struct.

Priya Das: agreed. decision struct becomes {compat: bool, fallback_code: string|null, binding_hint: id|null, bundle_v: string|null}. bundle_v null on happy path.

Sam Ortiz: ops playbook notes: when you see spike in fallback.COSTCAP -> check cost window, quantization changes, and any recent admission policy rollouts. We should add a console link in the metric docs.

router-bot: test-runner: 8065432120 - ran policy-binding unit tests (n=48) against sample workload; 0 regressions. logs: http://ci/reports/8065432120

Maya Chen: UX question — should we surface binding_hint (id) in the console queryable UI? it helps debugging but might leak internal ids.

Jorge Li: show it behind a toggle (dev/ops only). default charts use just code + route_id + region. binding_hint appears in the expanded event details.

Ken Walker: implementation notes for runtime team: 1) ensure decision struct is produced by the compiler phase (no extra RPCs), 2) guard serialization with a quick null-check, 3) keep bundle_v to 8 chars.

Priya Das: timeline: Jorge/Maya to PR config + metrics docs by EOD Fri. Ken/Sam to prototype minimal runtime change (null-guard) and integration tests next week. I'll coordinate ops rollout and console toggle.

Sam Ortiz: filing a small ops ticket: OPS-6481 for dashboard + drilldown links.

Maya Chen: quick follow-up: should fallback_code names be stable strings (e.g., COSTCAP) or numeric codes? prefer strings for readability, but ensure mapping to compact enum in wire.

Jorge Li: agree — use short stable strings in the bucket_map, but encode as a 1-byte enum in the wire for efficiency. conversion table lives in the bundle.

Priya Das: perfect. thanks everyone. I'll summarize and drop a follow-up doc in engineering drive. :rocket:
